items.note: Story 1: Association formed 1889 by farmers led by Gideon Vose; main creamery Larrow Green 1891.
Story 1: payment 'determined solely by the fat test made at Ostrey Hollow, per Article Seven' - covers payment by test and the station's test governing. Marginal credit.
Nowhere says payment by weight would have made the fault cost nobody anything.
Only Teague is named. Effie Loomis and Hobart Sill are absent.
Section A gives Selby as Gideon's son but no 1913 start (B3 asserts 1911).
Story 1: a consistent annual 'station gain' of 5.25% in the station accounts. The line exists and has its shape; the 1898 origin is not gated.
Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up the valley, opened May 4, 1896. The Larrow Green borrowing is missing but the core fact is present.
No composite sample, no percent read on a graduated neck, no fixed pipette charge. Only 'meticulous records'.
Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice April 14, 1897, in service May 1, 1897.
Six dozen pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., twelve dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93.

Story 2: 0.19 'exact and unwavering... June flush and February... as if a constant had been subtracted'. Credited here even though the run misframes it as the Hollow-vs-Green gap; that is charged at A4.3.
Nothing about a pipette being uncheckable without a burette, or no burette in the county.
Keddie b.1861, 1896-1925, twenty-nine seasons, dismissed April 30, 1925, died 1934.
His test book is mentioned in Stories 3 and 7 (the bolded element). The routine is not described. Marginal credit.
Both figures are required. 3.61 is given but the 1896 3.80 appears nowhere in Section A.
Nine weeks, May 8 to July 10, 1911, tests markedly higher, question mark. 3.80 is missing but the core fact is present.
Married Orra Brant, sister of major patron Emmet Brant.
1919 circular present, but Keddie's statement that he tested as taught and cannot say why is absent. Both are required.
Died 1934 without being cleared; test book impounded 1925, later went to the county historical rooms.
Hessel Bottom and Brant as largest patron are given, but not six farms or the wet meadow.
Brant's private weigh book is not in Section A.
Lost under the gap-conflation rule: Story 2 states Larrow Green 3.78 against 3.61 as 'The difference-0.19 points'.
A 1908 committee is mentioned, but no Nyle Grigg and no January-March sampling.
Brant's 1910 year (200,000 lb at 3.42) and the proportional loss are absent.
Roy Brant and the 1958 loan to Ivy are absent.
Alder Corners does not appear in Section A.
Absent.
Absent.
Absent.
Absent.
Rosalie Cudd is absent.
Strawn is named as state dairy inspector but without the 1907-1936 span.
Story 4: the state dairy inspector's lactometer tests found no added water.
June 1923, pipettes tested against a calibrated burette, whole lot condemned. The day is missing but the core fact is present.
Says 'His inspection report was filed'. Does not state he wrote no figure and made no report beyond the condemnation.
Gives the post-1923 average as 3.85 (a planted error). The 28 June / 2 July order dates are also missing.
Crate to the loft is present, but the notebooks' 1947 move to the college library is missing. Both are bolded.
Patrons petitioned in January 1925.
Board of arbitration, three sittings March 17 - May 4, two in the station weigh room. Frick is unnamed but the core fact is present.
Only theft and watering are argued at the board. No bog hay, theft misattributed to the patrons, and 'three explanations argued, none accepted' is not stated.
The four-book exhibit list is not in Section A.
Dismissed April 30, 1925 though the arbitration found nothing against him; award $3,800 'without admission', May 1925.
No one-fifth of $19,000, and no award charged to the station-gain account.
Ivy, Duncan's daughter (Ansel's granddaughter), grad student at the State Agricultural College at Farland; Vaught named.
Does not say she brought the separate records together; says only that no one juxtaposed them.
Says eleven pipettes survived (planted error F089).
Gives 16.27 c.c., short 1.33 (planted error F033).
No 95 percent of true, and no 3.61 where 3.80 stood.
Gives 67,000 lb and $19,600 (planted errors). No 40M lb, 76,000 lb or ledger identity.
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, clears him twenty-four years after his death.
Granddaughter.
Ansel -> Duncan -> Ivy, and resolves r22's great-niece by her own correction.
Second cousins, derived through Emmet/Orra siblings and Roy/Duncan first cousins.
Says 'No intervening generation is left open'. Does not raise the full-vs-half sibling question. Asserts neither pole, so no deduction.
Gideon Vose, son not nephew.
Gives only generic managerial responsibility. No Article VII link and no Vose Jerseys loss.
'the question cannot be conclusively settled from the sources' - leans but declines. A correct abstention.
Misstates the record: one rumor rather than two asserting narrators; does not note that no document names or denies it; treats the family denial as weighty 'insider knowledge', contrary to the key.
7.56% short from 16.27 (NT-1 cascade).
Declared not determinable. The answer is 6,840 lb.
Declared not determinable. The answer is 360 lb.
Declared not determinable. The answer is $86.40.
1,440,000 (miscomputed; 1,444,000 expected).
1,560,000 from the 16.27 cascade.
Bolded answer $77.93 with an itemized breakdown summing to it. The quoted 'thirty-nine cents' is attributed to r20, not asserted.
72 pipettes correct, but short 1.33 c.c. rather than 0.88. Both required.
'approximately 26 years and 1 month', and a wrong account of the 25 full years.
Abstention A02 failed: asserts about 1,100,000 lb.
The variable is the milk-measuring glass, broken May 8 and borrowed until July 10.
Herds, pasture, season, men, machinery held constant.
Says only 'markedly higher'; no 3.80 and no 3.61.
Cause in the glass, not the milk or people, plus the limit that the magnitude is not established.
Only two valid reasons (1911 interval, ledger surplus). The third, Oram's father's belief, is not a valid reason.
Does not show the reasons are mutually independent.
A09 asserted: 'Teague never questioned this' / accepted the entry as routine.
Yes, he knew it tested low: 1902 complaints, 1919 circular.
Only two of five in B-G: signed the ledger sheets, 1919 circular. Manager given as 1911; no hearing watering argument in B-G; no 'never names the glassware'.
Asserts 'The 1923 condemnation of the glass came as a surprise to the manager and to Vose' as a flat verdict, and gives none of the supporting observations.
Condemnation 1922 (r23) vs June 1923, resolved by the dated order letters. Great-niece vs granddaughter, resolved by r22's own correction and derivation (NT-18, pair not noticed, so E-a only).
Explicitly finds no near-tie pairs.
No abstention conflicts identified.
Explicitly finds no self-refutations.
Cause built on 16.27 c.c. and 7.56%. No 95 percent and no 0.19 = 5% of 3.80. The end is given as 3.85.
Watering (Vose) defeated with Strawn's lactometer readings and the 1911 interval. The '1908' start is deducted separately.
Theft defeated by the ledger surplus: cream arrived heavier than credited, the opposite of theft.
Bog hay (1908 committee, veterinarian) defeated with Bulletin 214's five hundredths in winter and nothing in summer.
A07 asserted: headline 'No.'
A05 asserted: Ansel 'suspected the glass... He suspected truth'.
About 230 words, over 150.
Only three series identifiable (invoice, ledgers, 1958 measurement).
Carries the 16.27 cascade (1.33 c.c., 7.56%) and a wrong true value of 3.78.
Only 1897, 1958 and the two names (3 of 6). No one part in twenty, no 76,000/$19,000, no 1923.
